blocks.text: AI 模型偏好变化之快前所未有

inlines.text: AI 模型偏好变化之快前所未有

blocks.text: 企业正越来越多地在模型版本和提供商之间迁移工作负载。今年年中，大多数组织的主要工作依赖少数几款 Anthropic 模型。如今，采用情况在模型版本和提供商之间都分散得多。同期，OpenAI 在企业 token 流量中的份额显著增长，主要得益于其 6 系列 Sol 和 Astra 模型。不过，模型质量仍然强烈影响提供商的市场份额；Claude Opus 5.5 发布后，势头又转回了 Anthropic。短短六周内，Opus 5.5 在闭源模型 token 中的占比从 7.2% 飙升至 37.9%，推动 Anthropic 的整体份额从 57.6% 升至 68.8%。

inlines.text: 企业正越来越多地在模型版本和提供商之间迁移工作负载。今年年中，大多数组织的主要工作依赖少数几款 Anthropic 模型。如今，采用情况在模型版本和提供商之间都分散得多。同期，OpenAI 在企业 token 流量中的份额显著增长，主要得益于其 6 系列 Sol 和 Astra 模型。不过，模型质量仍然强烈影响提供商的市场份额；Claude Opus 5.5 发布后，势头又转回了 Anthropic。短短六周内，Opus 5.5 在闭源模型 token 中的占比从 7.2% 飙升至 37.9%，推动 Anthropic 的整体份额从 57.6% 升至 68.8%。

blocks.text: 这种在模型和供应商之间灵活切换负载的模式，与 Databricks 自身的 AI 战略高度契合——我们一直快速评估并上线新模型。两个月前，我们推出了一套内部的首日模型上线流程，让我们能在几天内完成对新版本的评估。这套流程帮助我们在控制成本的同时提升了内部 AI 工作的质量。例如，我们发现 Opus 5.5 相比上一代，每次会话的质量更高、成本低 29%，这为我们决定将其设为 Claude Code 的默认模型提供了依据。

blocks.text: 企业正日益走出单一 AI 供应商的格局。就在今年 7 月，使用 Unity Gateway 的企业中约有 64% 只依赖一家模型供应商。到 11 月 2 日，这一比例已降至 28%，更多组织开始采用两家或更多供应商的模型。

blocks.text: 与此同时，开放权重模型也在稳步扩大份额。其占企业 token 流量的比例从 7 月的 7.3% 升至 11 月的 30.9%，不到四个月增长了三倍多。开放权重模型的竞争力也在不断增强，逐渐逼近专有模型。在我们的编码质量基准测试中，有三款开放权重模型跻身前十，其中 DeepSeek V4.1 和 GLM 5.3 以 93.1% 的通过率并列第三。正如我们在开放权重模型研究中所探讨的，这些模型不断提升的能力、成本效率和灵活性，正使其成为对企业越来越有吸引力的选择。

blocks.text: 选择合适的编码智能体，意味着要同时评估模型和运行它的框架。我们最新的编码智能体基准测试覆盖了九家 AI 实验室的模型，分别使用 Claude Code 和 Codex 运行。来自四家实验室（OpenAI、DeepSeek、Meta 和 Anthropic）的五款模型位于成本-质量前沿，在任务成功率和成本之间取得了最佳平衡。

blocks.text: 这些结果说明，单看模型排名并不能反映全貌。企业需要结合自身工作负载来评估模型与框架的组合，利用真实使用数据和调用轨迹来理解性能与成本之间的权衡。

blocks.text: 我们在 Databricks 内部就是这么做的。在评估是否要从 Opus 4.8 升级到 Opus 5 时，我们分析了成本-质量的帕累托前沿，并回放了自身工作负载的调用轨迹。结果显示，对我们的用例而言，这次升级不值得额外付出的成本，因此我们决定继续使用 4.8。

blocks.text: token 价格并不能说明 AI 编码成本的全貌

inlines.text: token 价格并不能说明 AI 编码成本的全貌

blocks.text: 两款模型可能跑出几乎相同的基准成绩，成本却相差悬殊。在我们的编码基准测试中，GPT-6 Luna 和 Claude Opus 5.5 的任务成功率均为 89.1%。但 Luna 平均每个任务仅花费 0.05 美元，而 Opus 5.5 为 1.62 美元，相差约 32 倍。

inlines.text: 两款模型可能跑出几乎相同的基准成绩，成本却相差悬殊。在我们的编码基准测试中，GPT-6 Luna 和 Claude Opus 5.5 的任务成功率均为 89.1%。但 Luna 平均每个任务仅花费 0.05 美元，而 Opus 5.5 为 1.62 美元，相差约 32 倍。

blocks.text: 每个任务的成本既取决于 token 价格，也取决于模型为得出答案所需的工作量。额外的轮次、冗长的输出和失败的尝试都会推高成本。Gemini 3.8 Flash 的 token 价格很低，但平均每个任务要跑 140 轮，最终以每个任务 11.97 美元成为基准测试中最贵的模型之一。对编码智能体而言，当模型需要更多步骤才能完成任务时，更低的 token 价格并不保证更低的成本。

blocks.text: 性能最强的 AI 模型往往并非性价比最高的选择

inlines.text: 性能最强的 AI 模型往往并非性价比最高的选择

blocks.text: 更高的基准测试成绩往往要付出高昂代价，哪怕质量只提升一点，成本也可能很高。Claude Fable 5.1 以 96.0% 的任务成功率登顶我们的基准测试，但每项任务成本为 7.47 美元；Muse Wonder 得分 94.9%，每项任务仅需 1.53 美元。多出的这 1.1 个百分点性能，代价接近五倍。企业似乎也认同这一点：自发布以来的 6 周里，Fable 5.1 在专有模型 token 中的份额从 5.5% 降到了 0.6%。

blocks.text: 对企业来说，问题在于一项任务究竟需要多高的质量。对于复杂、高风险的工作，高端模型值得付出这个成本；但常规任务用更便宜的替代方案可能就够了。智能模型路由，比如 Unity Gateway 中的 Smart Routing，可以根据质量和成本把任务匹配到合适的模型。

blocks.text: 什么是 Databricks AI Index？

inlines.text: 什么是 Databricks AI Index？

blocks.text: Databricks AI Index 是一个公开资源，用于追踪企业 AI 模型的采用情况、支出趋势和编程智能体性能。它结合了来自数千家使用 Databricks Unity Gateway 的企业的聚合匿名使用数据，以及基于真实开发任务的编程智能体基准测试。随着新模型接受评测，该指数每周更新。

inlines.text: Databricks AI Index 是一个公开资源，用于追踪企业 AI 模型的采用情况、支出趋势和编程智能体性能。它结合了来自数千家使用 Databricks Unity Gateway 的企业的聚合匿名使用数据，以及基于真实开发任务的编程智能体基准测试。随着新模型接受评测，该指数每周更新。

blocks.text: 如何比较用于编程任务的 AI 模型？

inlines.text: 如何比较用于编程任务的 AI 模型？

blocks.text: 比较用于编程的 AI 模型时，应看任务成功率、单任务成本，以及在不同编程智能体运行框架下的表现。Databricks AI Index 使用 Databricks 私有代码库中的真实编程工作流和隐藏测试，评测模型与运行框架的组合，以衡量质量和成本。结果会因工作负载而异，因此企业还应针对自己的开发任务评测模型。

blocks.text: 为什么更便宜的 AI 模型使用成本可能更高？

inlines.text: 为什么更便宜的 AI 模型使用成本可能更高？

blocks.text: 更低的 token 价格并不总能带来更低的成本，因为不同模型完成任务所需的工作量不同。需要更多推理轮次、生成更长输出或反复尝试的模型，总体上可能消耗更多 token。衡量 AI 效率时，完成单个任务的成本往往比单纯的 token 价格更有用。

blocks.text: 开放权重 AI 模型能与专有模型竞争吗？

inlines.text: 开放权重 AI 模型能与专有模型竞争吗？

blocks.text: 可以，开放权重 AI 模型在编程性能和成本效率上正越来越有竞争力。在 Databricks AI Index 的编程基准测试中，有三个开放权重模型进入任务成功率前 10 名，其中 DeepSeek V4.1 达到 93.1%。最佳选择取决于工作负载、所需质量和成本。

blocks.text: 企业如何优化 AI 模型选择和支出？

inlines.text: 企业如何优化 AI 模型选择和支出？

blocks.text: 企业可以通过在自身工作负载上比较模型质量和成本、监控使用情况，并根据任务需求选择模型来优化 AI 成本。Databricks Unity Gateway 提供集中式模型访问、使用仪表盘、统一追踪和预算功能，帮助组织管理 AI 支出。其智能路由能力还可以根据质量和性能，将编程智能体任务匹配到高性价比的模型。

blocks.text: The Index combines two complementary sources of data:

inlines.text: The Index combines two complementary sources of data:

blocks.text: Enterprise AI usage and spending. Aggregated, anonymized data from 10,000+ companies using Unity Gateway, spanning digital natives, Fortune 500, and Global 2000 enterprises, including traffic to external providers such as Anthropic and OpenAI. The Index tracks model adoption through token and spend shares across proprietary and open-weight models, as well as weekly AI spending patterns for individual users.

blocks.text: Continuously updated coding-agent evaluations. Building on the coding-agent benchmark we published in July, our latest evaluations draw on real coding-agent workflows from Databricks engineers, captured through Unity Gateway. These workflows span creating and reviewing pull requests, investigating issues, and tackling complex development tasks. Using tasks from our private codebase and withheld tests helps reduce the risk of benchmark contamination while enabling consistent comparisons of model-harness combinations and terms of task success rates and cost per completed task.

blocks.text: AI model preferences are changing faster than ever

inlines.text: AI model preferences are changing faster than ever

blocks.text: Enterprises are increasingly shifting workloads between model versions and providers. At mid-year, most organizations relied on a handful of Anthropic models for the majority of their work. Today, adoption is far more fragmented across model versions and providers alike. OpenAI's share of enterprise token traffic grew meaningfully over this period, driven largely by its 6 series Sol and Astra models. However, model quality continues to strongly influence provider market share; when Claude Opus 5.5 launched, momentum shifted back to Anthropic. In just six weeks, Opus 5.5 surged from 7.2% to 37.9% of proprietary-model tokens, lifting Anthropic's overall share from 57.6% to 68.8%.

blocks.text: The pattern of shifting workloads between models and providers aggressively matches our own AI strategy at Databricks, where we quickly evaluate and roll out new models. Two months ago, we introduced an internal Day 1 model rollout process which lets us evaluate new releases within days. This process has helped us manage cost while increasing the quality of internal AI efforts. For example, we found Opus 5.5 delivered improved quality at 29% lower cost per session than its predecessor, helping inform our decision to make it the default model for Claude Code.

blocks.text: Enterprises are embracing multi-AI and open-weight models

inlines.text: Enterprises are embracing multi-AI and open-weight models

blocks.text: Enterprises are increasingly moving beyond a single AI provider. As recent as July, approximately 64% of enterprises using Unity Gateway relied on just one model provider. By November 2, that had fallen to 28% as more organizations adopted models from more 2 or more providers.

blocks.text: Open-weight models are gaining ground alongside this shift. Their share of enterprise token traffic grew from 7.3% in July to 30.9% in November, more than quadrupling in less than four months. Open-weight models are also becoming increasingly competitive with proprietary alternatives. In our coding quality benchmark, three open-weight models rank among the top 10, including DeepSeek V4.1 and GLM 5.3, which both rank third with a 93.1% pass rate. As we explored in our research on open-weight models, their growing capabilities, cost efficiency, and flexibility are making them an increasingly attractive option for enterprises.

blocks.text: No single model or harness dominates the cost-quality frontier

inlines.text: No single model or harness dominates the cost-quality frontier

blocks.text: Choosing the right coding agent means evaluating both the model and the harness running it. Our latest coding-agent benchmark evaluates models across nine AI labs using Claude Code and Codex. Five models from four labs (OpenAI, DeepSeek, Meta, and Anthropic) sit on the cost-quality frontier, delivering the best trade-offs between task success rates and cost.

blocks.text: The results show why model rankings alone don't tell the full story. Enterprises need to evaluate model and harness combinations against their own workloads, using real usage data and traces to understand the trade-offs between performance and cost.

blocks.text: We use this approach internally at Databricks. When evaluating whether to upgrade from Opus 4.8 to Opus 5, we analyzed the cost-quality Pareto frontier and replayed traces from our own workloads. The results showed the upgrade wasn't worth the additional cost for our use cases, so we decided to stay on 4.8.

blocks.text: Token prices don't tell the full story of AI coding costs

inlines.text: Token prices don't tell the full story of AI coding costs

blocks.text: Two models can deliver nearly the same benchmark performance at dramatically different costs. In our coding benchmark, GPT-6 Luna and Claude Opus 5.5 both achieved an 89.1% task success rate. However, Luna averaged just $0.05 per task compared with $1.62 for Opus 5.5, a roughly 32x difference.

In our coding benchmark, GPT-6 Luna and Claude Opus 5.5 both achieved an 89.1% task success rate. However, Luna averaged just $0.05 per task compared with $1.62 for Opus 5.5, a roughly 32x difference.

blocks.text: Cost per task depends on both token prices and the amount of work a model must do to reach an answer. Extra turns, long outputs and failed attempts all increase cost. Gemini 3.8 Flash has a low token price, yet it averaged 140 turns per task and finished as one of the most expensive models in the benchmark at $11.97 per task. For coding agents, lower token prices don't guarantee lower costs when models require more work to complete a task.

blocks.text: The highest-performing AI model is rarely the best value

inlines.text: The highest-performing AI model is rarely the best value

blocks.text: Higher benchmark performance often comes at a steep price, and even small improvements in quality can carry high costs. Claude Fable 5.1 tops our benchmark with a 96.0% task success rate at $7.47 per task, while Muse Wonder scores 94.9% at just $1.53. That additional 1.1 percentage points of performance comes at nearly five times the cost. Enterprises appear to agree, and we saw Fable 5.1's share of proprietary tokens fall from 5.5% to 0.6% over 6 weeks since its launch.

blocks.text: The question for enterprises is how much additional quality a task actually requires. Premium models can be worth the cost for complex, high-stakes work, but less expensive alternatives may be sufficient for routine tasks. Intelligent model routing, such as Smart Routing in Unity Gateway, can help match tasks to appropriate models based on quality and cost.

blocks.text: AI spending is still highly concentrated

inlines.text: AI spending is still highly concentrated

blocks.text: AI spending varies dramatically across enterprise users. A developer running coding agents throughout the day has very different consumption patterns from those of an employee who asks an AI assistant a few questions a day. Our data highlights the stark difference: the median user spent just $2.49 on AI, while the 99th-percentile user spent $699.74, roughly 281x more.

blocks.text: About the data

inlines.text: About the data

blocks.text: The Databricks AI Index combines aggregated, anonymized usage data from thousands of enterprises using Unity Gateway with coding agent benchmarks based on real pull requests from Databricks' private codebase. Model spending is estimated using publicly listed provider prices, and benchmark results are evaluated against hidden tests rather than an LLM judge. Results reflect the workloads and models evaluated and may vary across organizations. The current dataset covers September 21 through November 7, 2026.

inlines.text: FAQs

blocks.text: What is the Databricks AI Index?

inlines.text: What is the Databricks AI Index?

blocks.text: The Databricks AI Index is a public resource tracking enterprise AI model adoption, spending trends, and coding agent performance. It combines aggregated, anonymized usage data from thousands of enterprises using Databricks Unity Gateway with coding agent benchmarks based on real development tasks. The Index is updated weekly as new models are evaluated.

blocks.text: How do you compare AI models for coding tasks?

inlines.text: How do you compare AI models for coding tasks?

blocks.text: AI models for coding should be compared on task success rate, cost per task, and performance within different coding agent harnesses. The Databricks AI Index evaluates model-harness combinations using real coding workflows from Databricks' private codebase and hidden tests to measure quality and cost. Results can vary by workload, so enterprises should also evaluate models against their own development tasks.

blocks.text: Why can cheaper AI models cost more to use?

inlines.text: Why can cheaper AI models cost more to use?

blocks.text: Lower token prices don't always translate to lower costs because models vary in how much work they need to complete a task. Models that require more reasoning turns, generate longer outputs, or make repeated attempts can consume more tokens overall. Cost per completed task is often a more useful measure of AI efficiency than token price alone.

blocks.text: Are open-weight AI models competitive with proprietary models?

inlines.text: Are open-weight AI models competitive with proprietary models?

blocks.text: Yes, open-weight AI models are increasingly competitive with proprietary models in coding performance and cost efficiency. In the Databricks AI Index coding benchmark, three open-weight models rank among the top 10 for task success rate, including DeepSeek V4.1 at 93.1%. The best choice depends on the workload, required quality, and cost.

blocks.text: How can enterprises optimize AI model selection and spending?

inlines.text: How can enterprises optimize AI model selection and spending?

blocks.text: Enterprises can optimize AI costs by comparing model quality and cost on their own workloads, monitoring usage, and selecting models based on task requirements. Databricks Unity Gateway provides centralized model access, usage dashboards, unified traces, and budgets to help organizations manage AI spending. Its Smart Routing capability can also match coding agent tasks to cost-effective models based on quality and performance.
